en.LevelSelect_Intro1: <color=#1B1212>A rip in the Space-Time Continuum has occured! I believe more will happen as a result.</color>
en.TTS_LevelSelect_Intro1: A rip in the Space-Time Continuum has occured! I believe more will happen as a result.
en.LevelSelect_Intro2: Lets travel to 1790s America. George Washington needs our help!
en.Guide_Bot_01: You've landed in 1793-America's caught between France and Britain. France insists that we assist them with their war with Great Britain.
en.Guide_Bot_02: As per our treaty from 1778, we are obligated to assist! George Washington knows the U.S. is not prepard to commit to any new wars right now.
en.Guide_Bot_03: Lets settle this with a friendly game of dodgeball! Remain neutral by taking as few hits as possible.
en.Guide_Bot_04: If your neutrality meter is below the half way point when the timer runs out, we will need to retry!
en.Guide_Bot_05: Watch out for your team mate. They agree we should go to war with Great Britain, so they will be trying to tilt the neutrality meter in their favor as well.
en.Dodgeball_Washington_01: Peace is fragile. I must choose wisely-for the sake of the nation.
en.Dodgeball_Jefferson_01: France stood with us. Now we stand with them!
en.Dodgeball_Hamilton_01: Neutrality is cowardice dressed as caution.
en.LevelSelect_XYZ1: After George Washington left presidential office John Adams took over.
en.LevelSelect_XYZ2: Adams still pursued peace with France, and was met with incredible difficulty.
en.LevelSelect_XYZ3: In 1793 he sent a peace envoy to try to negotiate peace with France.
en.LevelSelect_XYZ4: France demanded tribute be paid before peace could be established.
en.LevelSelect_XYZ5: Agents, X, Y, and Z were sent to collect this tribute. The U.S. refused!
en.LevelSelect_XYZ6: A new rip in the Space-Time Continuum has occured during this event. We need to go to 1793 and ensure the U.S. doesn't pay tribute!
en.LevelSelect_QuasiWar_Intro1: After France demanded tribute people in the United States are furious. We need to help President John Adams attempt peace!
en.LevelSelect_QuasiWar_Intro2: He faces tremendous pressure from his fellow country men. Even his own wife suggests against peace with France!
en.LevelSelect_QuasiWar_Intro3: Adams dispatched a peace envoy to France with hopes of negotiations in 1800. We need to make sure they get there unscathed!
en.LevelSelect_Quasi_Return1: John Adams has sent a group of brave men to France in hopes of establishing peace. We need to help them get there! Lets go!
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro1: Pirates off the North African coast are seizing American ships.
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro2: Before independence, American ships were protected by the British Royal Navy. After 1776, they became easy targets.
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro3: The Barbary States demanded tribute payments for safe passage for year. Thomas Jefferson is refusing!
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro4: Lets travel to 1804. In 1803, the USS Philadelphia ran aground and the crew was imprisoned!
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro5: Stephan Decatur burned the Philadelphia in Tripoli harbor to prevent its use by the enemy.
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Intro6: The time rip is threatening to thwart that effort! We must help him succeed!
en.LevelSelect_BarbaryWars_Return1: The shores of Tripoli echo with unfinished business. Time to set history straight!
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro1: The embargo sure stirred things up!
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro2: Great Britain is desperate to keep its navy fully staffed during this time.
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro3: By now Great Britain and France are at it again. In an effort to keep their navy strong they are snatching American sailors!
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro4: This was called Impressment. This is one of the many things that led us to the war of 1812!
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro6: The British Navy is prowling the harbor looking for deserters...even if they are Americans.
en.LevelSelect_Impressment_Intro7: You've got one shot to prove you're not one of them. Stay calm, stay sharp, and time your moves just right.
en.XYZ_Intro2: The Americans have just arrived. The French foreigh minister, Talleyrand has refused to speak to them.
en.XYZ_Intro3: Agents X, Y, and Z have just demanded tribute be paid!
en.XYZ_Intro4: In order to keep histroy from unravelling we must ensure he Americans do not pay 1 cent! Lets go!
en.Quasi_Intro1: Here we are in the 1800. France and the U.S., once allies are now on the brink of war.
en.Quasi_Intro2: You've boarded the USS Resolute, dispatched by President John Adams with 1 mission.
en.Quasi_Intro4: Dodge incoming French ships. Fire back if you must.
en.Quasi_Intro5: Your orders are clear. Your path is not.
en.Page1_Update1: ...the duty and interest of the United States require, that they should with sincerity and good faith adopt and pursue a conduct friendly and impartial toward the belligerent powers...
en.Page1_Update2: ...to terminate all differences and to establish a firm and lasting peace and friendship between His Majesty and the United States.
en.Page1_Update3: I am influenced by no diminution of zeal for your future interest… but retire from the great theater of action.
en.Page2_Update1: We attempted peace, but France wanted bribes.
en.Page2_Update2: If trouble is coming, we will face it with courage.
en.Page2_Update3: America stands for fairness and freedom. We will not be pushed around!
en.Page3_Update1: Congress gave us a Navy, and now we're fighting back at sea! - The Naval Act of 1798
en.Page3_Update2: We didn't declare war, but our ships are in battle! - Secretary of State Timothy Pickering's report to Congress
en.Page3_Update3: The enemy struck her colors after a spirited engagement. The American Flag was victorious! - Truxtun's offical battle report, 1799
en.Page4_Update2: The style of the demand admitted but one answer. I sent a small squadron of frigates... - Thomas Jefferson's message to Congress 1801
en.Page4_Update1: Tonight I watched Lieutenant Stephan Decatur lead a daring raid to burn the captured USS Philadelphia. The most bold and daring act of the age. - Admiral Horatio Nelson
en.Page4_Update3: The United States shall not be required to pay any further tribute. - Treaty of Peace and Amity with Tripoli, 1805
en.JournalInstruction: Swipe left or right to turn pages, or press the appropriate page turn button.
en.Dodge_Win_1: Congrtulations! George Washington was able to maintain neutrality.
en.Dodge_Win_2: You have unlocked the <u>Proclamation of Neutrality</u> in your journal.
en.Dodge_Win_2_TTS: You have unlocked the Proclamation of Neutrality in your journal.
en.Dodge_Lose_1: You were unable to maintain neutrality. We must go back and try again!
en.Dodgeball_R2_Win: One last chance to keep America out of Europe's endless wars and stand firm on neutrality!
en.Dodgeball_R2_Win2_TTS: You have unlocked Jay's Treaty in your journal.
en.Dodgeball_R2_Win2: You have unlocked <u>Jay's Treaty</u> in your journal.
en.Dodgeball_R3_Win: Washington said entangling alliances would drag this young nation into foreign wars. Neutrality wasn't just policy.
en.Dodgeball_R3_Win3: You have unlocked <u>Washington's Farewell Address</u> in your journal
en.Dodgeball_R3_Win3_TTS: You have unlocked Washington's Farewell Address in your journal
en.XYZ_WinRound1: Round 1 complete! You've unlocked a new journal entry.
en.XYZ_WinRound2: Round 2 complete! You've unlocked a new journal entry.
en.XYZ_WinRound3: That settles it! The U.S. has successfully refused to pay tribute.
en.Quasi_PopUp_Ally1: Millions for defense, not one cent for tribute!
en.Quasi_PopUp_Ally2: President Adams gave us a Navy. Lets show him it was worth it!
en.Quasi_PopUp_Ally3: Survive the storm. Peace talks are on the horizon!
en.Quasi_PopUp_Enemy2: Neutrality is cowardice! Choose a side!
en.Quasi_PopUp_Enemy3: We are not pirates! We are justice on the sea!
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival1: So, the Americans arrive. I trust your journey was...enlightening.
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival2: We come not with threats, but with hope that we can establish peace.
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival3: Peace is a luxury bought with strength. France does not bend to fear, but I respect courage. Your nation has shown it.
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival4: Your navy has harassed out ships for too long. We demand an end to hostilities and fair treatment on the seas.
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival5: Demand!? You are bold...but boldness built empires. Very well...France will honor peace if the United States honors neutrality.
en.QuasiCutscene_Arrival6: Tell your President: France does not seek war with republics born of revolution, but betray us, and the ocean will not protect you.
en.USSPhil: 1804: decatur leads a raid to burn the USS Philadelphia in Tripoli Harbor
en.Barbary_Phil1: Here we are. Lieutenant Decatur is already making his way to the Philadelphia.
en.Barbary_Phil2: Lets help him make it up here so he can set fire to the ship rendering it useless to the enemy!
en.Barbary_Phil3: Be careful to not be seen.
en.USSCaught: You have been caught! Your stealth was no match for their watchful eyes. The USS Philadelphia sails on...without you.
en.ShipBurn1: Boom! Thats one less ship in enemy hands.
en.ShipBurn2: The Philadelphia is destroyed and your daring act echoes through time.
en.ShipBurn3: After this, President Jefferson imposed an Embargo on ALL foreign trade.
en.ShipBurn4: He believed the U.S. could starve Great Britain and the Barabry Corsairs of trade.
en.ShipBurn5: Its time to travel to 1807 and ensure Jefferson's plan unfolds...however damaging it may be to the U.S. at the time. Histroy must remain accurate!
en.LevelSelect_Embargo1: With the Philadelphia in flames and tensions rising, the fight shifts from cannon fire to commerce.
en.LevelSelect_Embargo2: In 1807 President Thomas Jefferson signed the Embargo Act.
en.LevelSelect_Embargo3: This halted all US. exports and blocked ALL imports from foreign countries!
en.LevelSelect_Embargo4: Lets travel to 1807 and help Jefferson keep all foreign imports out!
en.Embargo_Intro1: We've landed at Baltimore Harbor in 1807.
en.Embargo_Intro2: President Jefferson's Embargo Act is in full swing. No foreign goods in or out.
en.Embargo_Intro3: Lets sort these packages out so that ONLY American goods are being traded domestically.
en.Embargo_Intro4: Click on foriegn crates to reject them. Be careful not to click any American crates!
en.Impressment_Guard1: You claim to be American? Prove it before I prove otherwise.
en.Impressment_Guard2: Impressment is lawful. Resistance is not.
en.Impressment_Guard3: You will find the King's service less forgiving than your merchant's
en.Impressment_Guard4: Speak up boy. The sea doesn't wait for cowards.
en.Impressment_Guard5: Your accent is slippery. Not quite colonial, not quite honest.
en.Impressment_Guard6: No papers? No protection. That makes you ours, lad.
en.Impressment_Guard7: You have the look of a deserter. Come with me now.
en.Impressment_Guard8: We have quotas to fill. Your story better be air tight.
en.Impressment_Intro1: Welcome to 1811. British naval commanders are on the look out for any able-bodied men they can illegally recruit into their navy.
en.Impressment_Intro2: Lets help this American get home over here without getting impressed!
en.Impress_Inst: Hold down the left mouse button to begin moving the arrow. Lift the left mouse button when the arrow is within the target zone to avoid impressment!
en.Impressment_Loss: You've been impressed into the British Royal Navy. We need to time warp back and try again!
en.LS_Mc1: You've seen the injustice of impressment first hand. American sailors have been stolen, silenced and forced to serve a foreign crown.
en.LS_Mc2: Now British warships gather near Baltimore. Their cannons aimed at Fort McHenry.
en.LS_Mc3: If the flag falls, so does the hope of a unified nation!
en.LS_Mc4: Your next and final mission: <u>Defend Fort McHenry.</u>
en.LS_Mc4_TTS: Your next and final mission: Defend Fort McHenry.
en.LS_Mc5: This battle is one of the most defining battles of the War of 1812.
en.LS_Mc6: We will need to travel to the year 1814 and hold the line against British bombardment to ensure the flag is still flying when its all said and done!
en.Mc_Intro1: September 13, 1814: The British Navy has positioned themselves just outside of Baltimore Harbor.
en.Mc_Intro2: The bombardment is soon to begin...
en.Mc_Intro3: They intend to break your will to persevere! Don't allow them to secure naval dominance in the Chesapeake Bay!
en.Mc_Intro4: Left click the cannon balls as they come flying towards Ft. McHenry to stop them from reaching their target and survive until the timer runs down!
en.LevelSelect_Complete1: Mission complete. The flag endures. You've done more than preserve the integrity of histroy. You've given back its heart beat.
en.LevelSelect_Complete2: I detect no more time rips in this era. We can leave this timeline open so you can return to any era and replay the moments that shaped history.
en.LevelSelect_Complete3: In the meantime, I will be leaving to ensure no other time rips exist in other eras. Feel free to join me when you're finished by selecting the Complete Game button at the bottom right of this screen.
en.Page5_Update1: The belligerent powers of Europe threaten our vessels. I have urged congress to consider the advantages of halting all departures from our ports. - Thomas Jefferson 1807
en.Page5_Update2: The docks are silent. My ships rot in the harbot. Their carggo unsold. Jefferson calls this patriotism. I call it strangulation! We've been punished for the crimes of foreign powers. - New England Merchant 1807
en.Page5_Update3: In every point of view I prefer a war to a permanent embargo. - Albert Gallatin to Jefferson, December 1807
en.Page6_Update1: The took me from the ship Chesapeake. I told them I was American, but they said I was a British subject and must serve. - Deposition of John Strachan, 1807
en.Page6_Update2: This act was a flagrant violation of our rights. I have issues a proclamation interdicting British armed vessels from our harbors. - Jefferson's Proclamation, 1807
en.Page6_Update3: The right of the king to the allegiance of his subjects is indefeasible. No act of a foreign state can discharge it. - British Foreign Office, 1807
en.Page7_Update1: By the dawn's early light...our flag was still there. - Franic Scott Key, The Defense of Fort McHenry, 1814
en.Page7_Update2: The flag was kept flying during the whole bombardment...though several shells struck flagstaff. - Major George Armistead, 1814
en.Page7_Update3: The fort was found too strong to be taken by bombardment. - Vice Admiral Alexander Cochrane, 1814
